record.title: Compatibility conjecture for the Grossman–Larson coproduct and rooted-tree coproduct
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be the Hopf algebra of rooted trees, let $H_{GL}$ be the Grossman–Larson Hopf algebra, and let $\Delta$ and $S_{GL}$ denote the relevant coproduct and antipode, with $\Delta_{GL}$ the coproduct transported to $H_{GL}$. For a linear map $m^{2,4}$ defined by

$$
m^{2,4}(a\otimes b\otimes c\otimes d)=a\otimes c\otimes bd,
$$

**Compatibility conjecture.** For any rooted tree $t$,

$$
(\Delta_{GL}\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal H})\circ\Delta(t)=m^{2,4}\circ(\Delta\otimes\Delta)\circ\Delta_{GL}(t)
$$

and

$$
\Delta\circ S_{GL}(t)=(S_{GL}\otimes\operatorname{id})\circ\Delta(t).
$$

These identities would give an analogue of the corresponding compatibility between the Kreimer and Grossman–Larson structures. The source presents them as a question, so their resolution is not established here.
record.source_name: Damien Calaque, Kurusch Ebrahimi-Fard and Dominique Manchon, “Two interacting Hopf algebras of trees”, arXiv:0806.2238 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2238

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

record.title: Recognition of edge-clique graphs
record.statement: An **edge-clique graph** is a graph obtained as the edge-clique graph $K_e(G)$ of some graph $G$, where vertices of $K_e(G)$ represent edges of $G$ and adjacency represents incident edges in $G$. **Recognition conjecture.** Determining whether a given graph is an edge-clique graph is an open problem. The paper notes that, as far as the authors know, no recognition algorithm or complexity classification is known.
record.source_name: Maw-Shang Chang, Ton Kloks and Ching-Hao Liu, “Edge-clique graphs of cocktail parties have unbounded rankwidth”, arXiv:1205.2483 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.2483

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2012). “As far as we know, the recognition of edge-clique graphs is an open problem.”

record.title: Collapsibility conjecture for nerve complexes of circular arcs
record.statement:
Let $l$, $n$, and $k$ be integers satisfying

$$
\frac{l}{l+1}<\frac{k}{n}<\frac{l+1}{l+2}.
$$

Let $\mathcal{N}({n},{k})$ be the nerve complex of the corresponding circular arcs, and let $\partial C_{2l+2}(n)$ denote its embedded sphere.

**Collapsibility conjecture.** The complex $\mathcal{N}({n},{k})$ simplicially collapses to $\partial C_{2l+2}(n)$.

The paper establishes that $\partial C_{2l+2}(n)$ is an embedded sphere whose fundamental class generates the relevant homology group. It remains open whether this embedded sphere is always a combinatorial deformation retract of $\mathcal{N}({n},{k})$; simplicial collapse would imply such a deformation retraction.
record.source_name: Michal Adamaszek, Henry Adams, Florian Frick, Chris Peterson and Corrine Previte-Johnson, “Nerve complexes of circular arcs”, arXiv:1410.4336 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.4336

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2014). “We leave it as an open problem whether the embedded sphere is always a combinatorial deformation retract of $\cnk{n}{k}$.”

record.title: Diversity bound for intersecting-free hypergraph families
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal F\subset {[n]\choose k}$ satisfy $\nu(\mathcal F)\leq s$ and $n\geq k(s+1)$. Define the $s$-diversity by

$$
\gamma_s(\mathcal F)=\min_T|\mathcal F(\bar T)|,
$$

where $\mathcal F(\bar T)=\\{F\in\mathcal F:F\cap T=\emptyset\\}$. **Diversity bound conjecture.** One has

$$
\gamma_s(\mathcal F)\leq\max\left\\{\sum_{l=2}^{s+1}{{s+1}\choose l}{{n-2s-1}\choose{k-l}},{{(k-1)(s+1)}\choose k}\right\\}.
$$

The conjecture asks for a sharp upper bound on the diversity of a family with matching number at most $s$. The source presents it as a question for further progress; no resolution status is supplied.
record.source_name: Peter Frankl and Andrey Kupavskii, “The Erdős Matching Conjecture and concentration inequalities”, arXiv:1806.08855 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.08855

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

record.title: Mutation connectivity conjecture for uniform matroid polytopes of rank 4
record.statement:
A **uniform matroid polytope of rank $4$** is a uniform matroid polytope with rank $4$. Consider two such matroid polytopes on the same ground set, and require every intermediate object in a mutation sequence to remain a matroid polytope.

**Mutation connectivity conjecture for uniform matroid polytopes.** Every pair of uniform matroid polytopes of rank $4$ on the same ground set can be transformed into each other by a finite number of mutations, preserving the matroid polytope property.

This problem is motivated by the Cordovil–Las Vergnas conjecture, which asserts mutation connectivity for uniform oriented matroids. The source presents the rank-$4$ matroid-polytope version as an open problem.
record.source_name: Hiroyuki Miyata, “A two-dimensional topological representation theorem for matroid polytopes of rank 4”, arXiv:1809.04236 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.04236

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2018). “Pseudosphere arrangements on $S^{r-1}$ ($r \geq 4$) are usually very difficult to visualize, and there remain many open problems on rank $r (\geq 4)$ oriented matroids.”

record.title: Finite generation conjecture for verbal subgroups
record.statement:
Let $w=w(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ be a group word and let $G$ be a profinite group. Write $G_w$ for the set of $w$-values in $G$, and let $w(G)$ denote the closed subgroup generated by those values.

**Finite generation conjecture.** If

$$
|G_w|<2^{\aleph_0},
$$

then $w(G)$ is generated by finitely many $w$-values.

This is presented as a weaker version of the strong conciseness conjecture. The paper does not establish it in general, although it follows in cases where strong conciseness is known together with the relevant finite-generation argument.
record.source_name: Eloisa Detomi, Benjamin Klopsch and Pavel Shumyatsky, “Strong conciseness in profinite groups”, arXiv:1907.01344 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.01344

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Linear bound conjecture for r-wise fractional L-intersecting families
record.statement:
Let $cmathcal{F}$ be an $r$-wise fractional $L$-intersecting family, where $L=\{a/b\}$. The family is **r-wise fractional L-intersecting** if every $r$ distinct members have pairwise fractional intersections in $L$. **Linear bound conjecture.** Then

$$
|\mathcal{F}| = \mathcal{O}\left((r-1)n \right).
$$

The paper currently proves an upper bound of order $\mathcal{O}\left((r-1)n\frac{\ln^2 n}{\ln\ln n}\right)$ in the singleton case; the conjectured linear bound remains open.
record.source_name: Tapas Kumar Mishra, “r-wise fractional L-intersecting family”, arXiv:1909.13217 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.13217

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2019). “We believe that in this case, $|\mathcal{F}| \in \Theta(n^s)$ and improving the bound in Theorem remains open.”

record.title: NP-completeness of the hull number problem for oriented chordal graphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph and let $k$ be a positive integer. The underlying graph of $D$ is the graph obtained by ignoring the orientations of its arcs.

**Oriented chordal hull-number conjecture.** Determining whether

$$
\overrightarrow{\operatorname{hn}}(D)\leq k
$$

is NP-complete, even when the underlying graph of $D$ is chordal.

This would extend the known NP-hardness of determining the hull number of an undirected chordal graph to oriented graphs. The source presents the claim as an open problem; its precise complexity for oriented graphs with chordal underlying graphs remains open.
record.source_name: Julio C. S. Araujo and Pedro S. M. Arraes, “Hull and Geodetic Numbers for Some Classes of Oriented Graphs”, arXiv:1911.10240 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10240

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2019). “Another open problem would be:”

record.title: Oboudi's comparability conjecture for trees under independence-polynomial order
record.statement:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be trees of order $n$. Write $T_1\triangleleft T_2$ when the independence polynomial order satisfies the strict relation, and $T_2\trianglelefteq T_1$ for the corresponding non-strict relation. **Oboudi's comparability conjecture.** Is it true that

$$
T_1\triangleleft T_2\quad\text{or}\quad T_2\trianglelefteq T_1?
$$

The question asks whether every pair of trees of the same order is comparable in this order; the paper presents an infinite family showing that the proposed comparability fails.
record.source_name: Iain Beaton and Ben Cameron, “On the largest real root of the independence polynomial of a unicyclic graph”, arXiv:2006.05511 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.05511

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The equivalence of finite-path perfect matching and \(\mathsf{ATR}_0\)
record.statement:
Let $athsf{PM}$ denote the perfect matching principle, and let $ext{Finite Path }\mathsf{PM}$ denote its restriction to finite-path instances. Let $peratorname{\mathsf{ATR}}_0$ and $peratorname{\mathsf{RCA}}_0$ be the indicated systems of reverse mathematics.

**Finite-path perfect matching conjecture.** $ext{Finite Path }\mathsf{PM}$ is equivalent to $peratorname{\mathsf{ATR}}_0$ over $peratorname{\mathsf{RCA}}_0$.

The paper proves that finite-path perfect matching is close in strength to $peratorname{\mathsf{ATR}}_0$ and asks whether it implies that system, as well as whether $peratorname{\mathsf{ATR}}_0$ proves finite-path perfect matching or perfect matching. The supplied text does not resolve these questions.
record.source_name: Stephen Flood, Matthew Jura, Oscar Levin and Tyler Markkanen, “The computational strength of matchings in countable graphs”, arXiv:2006.11334 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11334

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

record.title: Bucko–Czap conjecture on 1-planarity of lexicographic products
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $K_2$ denote the complete graph with two vertices. A graph is **1-planar** if it has a drawing in the plane in which every edge is crossed by at most one other edge. A **cactus** is a connected graph in which every edge belongs to at most one cycle. **Bucko–Czap's conjecture.** The graph $G\circ K_2$ is 1-planar if and only if $G$ is a cactus. This open problem characterizes 1-planarity for lexicographic products with $K_2$ and concerns the relationship between graph substitution and sparse crossing structures.
record.source_name: Licheng Zhang and Yuanqiu Huang, “The reducibility of optimal 1-planar graphs”, arXiv:2211.14733 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.14733

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2022). “So the study of 1-planarity of the lexicographic products of graphs only leaves the following open problem.”

record.title: The diversity bound for large intersecting families
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}\subset\binom{[n]}{k}$ be an intersecting family, where $n>100k$, and suppose that

$$
|\mathcal{F}|>\binom{n-3}{k-3}.
$$

Here $\varrho(\mathcal{F})$ denotes the diversity of $\mathcal{F}$. **The diversity bound conjecture.** Then

$$
\varrho(\mathcal{F})\geq\frac{3}{7}.
$$

This is posed as a challenging open problem concerning improved lower bounds on the diversity of large intersecting families. Its resolution is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Peter Frankl and Jian Wang, “Improved bounds on the maximum diversity of intersecting families”, arXiv:2304.11089 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11089

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2023). “Let us conclude this paper by a challenging open problem.”

record.title: Tournament path strengthening of the flash-and-rainbow conjecture
record.statement: Let $l$ and $k$ be positive integers, and let $T$ be a tournament with $l^{k-1}+1$ vertices. A directed monochromatic path has all edges of one colour, while a directed rainbow path has pairwise distinct edge colours. **Path strengthening.** Every edge-colouring of $T$ contains a directed monochromatic path of length $l$ or a directed rainbow path of length $k$. This is a more restrictive variant of the tournament conjecture, which in the paper is formulated for directed walks; the source presents this path version as an open possibility because directed cycles create additional technical difficulties.
record.source_name: António Girão, Freddie Illingworth, Lukas Michel, Michael Savery and Alex Scott, “Flashes and rainbows in tournaments”, arXiv:2305.13422 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13422

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

record.title: The ordinary diversity bound for intersecting uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}\subset \binom{[n]}{k}$ be an intersecting family, and let $\gamma(\mathcal{F})$ denote its ordinary diversity. Suppose that $n>4k$. **Ordinary diversity conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(\mathcal{F})\leq \binom{n-3}{k-2}.
$$

This is posed as an open problem concerning the ordinary diversity of intersecting families. It asks for a sharp upper bound under the linear condition $n>4k$; the supplied text does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Peter Frankl and Jian Wang, “On the C-diversity of intersecting hypergraphs”, arXiv:2308.14028 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1804.11269](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11269).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14028

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2023). “Let us conclude this paper by a open problem concerning the ordinary diversity.”

record.title: Quasisymmetric characteristic formula for a statistic-and-descent model
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an $\fS_n$-module, and let $X$ be a set of combinatorial objects equipped with functions $\operatorname{stat}:X\to\mathbb{N}$ and $\operatorname{set}:X\to\mathcal{P}(\{1,2,\ldots,n-1\})$. **Quasisymmetric characteristic formula conjecture.** Then

$$
F_{char}(M;q)=\sum_{x\in X}q^{\operatorname{stat}(x)}F_{\operatorname{set}(x)}.
$$

This is presented as a general form of open conjectures motivated by deforming symmetric-group modules into $\mathcal{H}_n(0)$-modules; the excerpt does not specify additional hypotheses relating $M$ and $X$.
record.source_name: Angela Hicks and Samantha Miller-Brown, “Three Examples of Quasisymmetric Compatible S_n-modules”, arXiv:2403.16249 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16249

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Canonical positive monomial expression conjecture for non-commutative Schur functions
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition of size $k$, and let $s_\lambda({\mathbf u})$ and $h_\lambda({\mathbf u})$ be the non-commutative Schur and homogeneous symmetric functions in the ribbon Schur operators $u_i$. A monomial is written as $\underline{u}=u_{i_k}u_{i_{k-1}}\cdots u_{i_1}$. **Canonical expression conjecture.** The functions $s_\lambda({\mathbf u})$ can be written as a non-negative sum of monomials, with a canonical expression obtained by selecting monomials occurring in $h_\lambda({\mathbf u})$; specifically, the selected monomials satisfy the strict inequalities within each consecutive block of indices determined by the parts of $\lambda$: 

$$
i_{\lambda_1}>i_{\lambda_1-1}>\cdots>i_1,
$$

$$
i_{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}>i_{\lambda_1+\lambda_2-1}>\cdots>i_{\lambda_1+1},
$$

and so on. This is proposed as the paper's main problem and would provide a canonical combinatorial explanation for the non-negativity of the associated skew $q$-Littlewood–Richardson coefficients.
record.source_name: Thomas Lam, “Ribbon Schur Operators”, arXiv:math/0409463 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0409463

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2004).

record.title: Zero forcing and path number under vertex sums
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs with an identified vertex $v$. Write $G\,\makebox[0ex][l]{$+$} \raisebox{-.75ex}{\makebox[2ex]{$_{v}$}}\,H$ for their vertex sum at $v$. Suppose that $Z(G)=P(G)$ and $Z(H)=P(H)$. **Vertex-sum conjecture.** Then

$$
Z(G\,\makebox[0ex][l]{$+$} \raisebox{-.75ex}{\makebox[2ex]{$_{v}$}}\,H)=P(G\,\makebox[0ex][l]{$+$} \raisebox{-.75ex}{\makebox[2ex]{$_{v}$}}\,H).
$$

This proposed closure property would provide a larger family of graphs for which the zero forcing number equals the path number, extending the known examples of block-cycle graphs. The source presents it as a problem for further study; its resolution is not given here.
record.source_name: Fatemeh Alinaghipour Taklimi, Shaun Fallat and Karen Meagher, “On the Relationships between Zero Forcing Numbers and Certain Graph Coverings”, arXiv:1311.7064 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.7064

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).

record.title: Extending Pseudosegment Arrangements by Subdivision
record.statement: How many intersections among an arrangement of pseudosegments in the plane must be added as vertices to allow the pseudosegment arrangment to be extended to a pseudoline arrangement? An arrangement of pseudosegments in the plane is a family of finite-length planar curves such that every two curves intersect in at most one point. An arrangement of pseudolines in the plane is a family of planar curves that extend to infinity on both ends such that every two curves intersect in at most one point. Only some pseudosegment arrangements can be extended to pseudoline arrangements. However, if we allow turning intersection points into vertices of the arrangement, thereby subdividing the segments, then it is always possible to make a pseudosegment arrangement extendible. The question is how many such vertices must be added in the worst-case in terms of the number $n$ of pseudosegments.
record.source_name: Open Problems Project - Computational Geometry

record.title: Erdős Problem #617 — Missing Colors in Complete-Graph Colorings
record.statement: Let $r\geq3$. If the edges of the complete graph $K_{r^2+1}$ are colored with $r$ colors, must there exist $r+1$ vertices such that one color is absent from all edges among those vertices? Equivalently, for every finite vertex set $V$ with $|V|=r^2+1$ and every coloring of the unordered pairs of vertices by the colors in $\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, there exist a subset $S\subseteq V$ with $|S|=r+1$ and a color $k$ such that no edge between two distinct vertices of $S$ has color $k$.
record.source_name: The Formal Conjectures Authors, Formal Conjectures (2025); independently edited from the pinned source file.

record.title: Erdős Problem #1199 — Monochromatic Sumsets in Two-Colorings
record.statement:
In every 2-coloring $c:\mathbb N\to\{0,1\}$, does there exist an infinite set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ such that all elements of its sumset
$$A+A=\{a+b:a,b\in A\}$$
have the same color? Equivalently, must there exist an infinite $A$ such that, for all $n,m\in A+A$, $c(n)=c(m)$?
record.source_name: The Formal Conjectures Authors, Formal Conjectures (2025); independently edited from the pinned source file.
